reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement. Amyloid PET SUVR showed significant reduction (-12.83 centiloids vs placebo, p<0.001), indicating BACE1 inhibition successfully reduced amyloid beta production. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The target was engaged and downstream biology changed as predicted - amyloid burden was reduced significantly. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite clear biological activity, clinical endpoints failed completely. CDR-SB showed no benefit (-0.17, p=0.385) and ADCOMS also failed (-0.02, p=0.345). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Even in the enriched subgroup with baseline amyloid PET SUVR 1.2-1.6, clinical endpoints remained negative (CDR-SB p=0.316, ADCOMS p=0.254). 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major confounders - adequate sample size (2212), appropriate duration (24 months), well-controlled trial. This is a classic 'biology moved, endpoint flat' failure where the mechanism worked but didn't translate to clinical benefit.
